history.period: Ancient; literary references from 6th century BCE; current structures 18th-20th century
history.summary: THIS IS A JAIN TIRTHA (PILGRIMAGE SITE), NOT A HINDU TEMPLE - keep-or-drop decision needed. Sammed Shikharji ('peak of concentration') on Parasnath Hill (1,365 m, the highest mountain in Jharkhand) is the most important Jain tirtha: 20 of the 24 Tirthankaras, including Parshvanatha (the 23rd, whose name gives the hill 'Parasnath'), attained moksha here. The earliest literary mention is in the Jnatrdharmakatha (6th century BCE); a 13th-century palm-leaf manuscript depicts Parshvanatha's nirvana here. There are 31 tonks (shrines) across the hill, the main one being the Jal Mandir surrounded by a water tank; idol inscriptions date to 1678 AD. Revered by both Digambara and Shvetambara sects. NOTE: CSV town 'Parasnath' is the hill's name; the base town is Madhuban (town corrected). The Santhal community also holds the hill sacred as Marang Buru.

name: Shikharji Temple (Teerthraj Shikharji)
town_description: Madhuban is the base town of the Sammed Shikharji yatra in Giridih district, at the foot of Parasnath Hill on the Delhi-Kolkata Grand Trunk Road (NH-2). The pilgrimage involves a roughly 27-km round trek visiting all 31 tonks, done on foot or by doli (palanquin). The surrounding Madhuvan forest makes it a serene, inward-looking rural town.
